newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN FASTEST AS WILLIAMS RAISE TEMPO.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN FASTEST AS WILLIAMS RAISE TEMPO.

text.p: Three weeks after a disappointing exit from the Australian Grand Prix, Heinz-Harald Frentzen responded on Friday in the best possible fashion by dominating opening practice for Sunday's Brazilian race.

On a hot day at the sprawling Interlagos circuit in the suburbs of Sao Paulo, the soft-spoken German outpaced Williams team mate and world championship favourite Jacques Villeneuve of Canada by three-tenths of a second.

Frentzen clocked a best time of one minute 17.506 seconds with a lap that endorsed a widespread feeling that he is both fast enough, and resilient enough, to raise a powerful challenge to his team-mate this year.
Many observers had suggested, particularly after he spun off with two laps left when in second place in Australia, that Frentzen may struggle to live up to expectations as a Williams driver.

But he put that notion to rest on Friday as the Williams duo grabbed the top two positions in a show of strength that suggested they have every prospect of doing the same, both in qualifying and in Sunday's 72-lap race.

Frentzen was reserved about his chances for the rest of the weekend. "I think this track has always been good for Williams in the past and I am working on a number of different set-ups. I am looking forward to tomorrow, when I can have another go.
"But I know that today is only practice -- so although I am ahead of Jacques, and that feels nice, I am not counting on anything at all.
"In Australia, when I was in front in the race, I think I showed a lot of people that I am capable of doing this job and I feel better for that. It was a good thing for me."
Villeneuve said: "We seem to have made some progress. I think the track was a bit dirty today as there have been other cars on it this weekend to help clean it up. But I am confident."
For the Williams team, a return to form is imperative after both cars failed to finish a race won by Briton David Coulthard in a McLaren.

On Friday, Coulthard was down in eighth place -- just one ahead of defending world champion and fellow-Briton Damon Hill in his improved Arrows -- as the times suggested a more expected order of affairs.
Hill was delighted with the vastly improved performance of his Arrows car and far more optimistic.
"I think it has been a good day for me. We got nearly all our laps in for one thing and we are looking reasonably competitive. We have got a lot of work done.
"I am more optimistic. It is always good for morale to get in the top ten and to be looking competitive, but I know also that Friday is a difficult day to assess.
"We have a lot of information to work through and we know where we stand. I think there is a good chance we can be in the top 10 in qualifying. If we could do that, it would be tremendous."
Frenchman Jean Alesi in a Benetton was third fastest with team mate Gerhard Berger of Austria fifth, the pair split by the fastest Briton Johnny Herbert in a Sauber.
Ralf Schumacher of Germany in a Jordan outpaced his brother Michael in a Ferrari as they filled sixth and seventh places on a day when something like normal service was resumed.
